hook_text: A picture lies about angles. Three flat views tell the truth. Here is where they go.
clip_script: Put a block in a glass box. Look through the front: width and height. Look down through the top: width and depth. Look through the left end: depth and height. Each view is true, no squashed angles, every size real. Now the first angle pattern: front view first, top view straight underneath, and the left end view on the right, because the view falls on the pane beyond the block. Join them with feint lines and leave the lines in. Cut a step across the top front of a 60 cube: front view, a square with a line 40 up; side view, an L; top view, a square with a line 20 from the front. Read the three together and the solid block appears in your head.
visual_style: Whiteboard glass box unfolding into three aligned rectangles; a stepped cube's three views drawn with feint projection lines joining them.
pacing: Glass box in ten seconds, pattern rule, stepped cube example, the read-together payoff.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the three views of a matchbox with a corner cut off.
